topic: Why Utility Stores Corporation shut down for good in 2025
why_it_works: USC only started losing money the year its subsidy was withdrawn under the IMF program — the government then cited those losses as the reason to shut the whole chain down, turning a policy choice into an 'operational failure' story, the same pattern now playing out with circular debt and DISCO privatization.
hook_angle: Contradiction hook: 'The government shut down Utility Stores for losing money. Utility Stores only started losing money once the government stopped subsidizing it.'

topic: Circular debt: why it keeps growing even after every government promises to fix it
why_it_works: In 2025 banks and government signed a 'landmark' Rs1.225 trillion deal to resolve circular debt — and the very next fiscal year it grew by another Rs364 billion anyway, because the deal restructured the existing debt stock without touching the two things that generate new debt every year: DISCO losses and take-or-pay capacity payments to IPPs.
hook_angle: Contradiction hook: 'In 2025, Pakistan signed a landmark deal to finally resolve circular debt. The next fiscal year, it grew anyway.'
sources: Pakistan Banks Association (2025 circular debt resolution deal); Express Tribune/Shafaqna (Rs364bn FY25-26 rise); Profit by Pakistan Today (Rs1.84tn by Feb 2026); IEEFA (capacity payments crisis); EnergyUpdate (18 May 2026, take-and-pay renegotiation); CRSS/ADB/PACRA (mechanism background)
notes: Full script drafted at content/scripts/2026-08-17-circular-debt.md. Open items: reconcile the Rs364bn net figure against individually-reported contributing factors and subsidies against a primary NEPRA/Ministry of Finance source; confirm FY26 update to the Rs1.81tn capacity payment figure; verify the 10% Debt Service Surcharge terms against NEPRA's own determination.

topic: What China actually gets from the 2026 CPEC revamp and Gwadar expansion
why_it_works: Xi and Shehbaz Sharif announced a 'new broad consensus' on CPEC and Gwadar in May 2026 — framed publicly as connectivity and development, but Pakistan owes China roughly $30B of its $124B external debt, and Gwadar sits inside China's wider String-of-Pearls port network, so the real question is what leverage this creates, not just what gets built.
sources: Al Jazeera - Pakistan and China reach new broad consensus (May 2026); Modern Diplomacy - China and Pakistan agree to revamp CPEC and expand Gwadar; debt figures need primary-source (SBP/Ministry of Finance) verification

topic: Pakistan is about to privatize its power distribution companies for the first time — what's actually being sold off
why_it_works: The government is selling FESCO, GEPCO, and IESCO first — the DISCOs with the LOWEST losses, not the worst offenders (PESCO/SEPCO) — a contradiction that reveals the deal is shaped by what's commercially sellable under IMF deadline pressure, not by what's most broken.
hook_angle: Contradiction hook: 'You'd guess Pakistan would privatize its worst power companies first. It's selling the better ones instead.'
sources: ProPakistani (16 Jul 2026, 18 Mar 2026); NEPRA 2025 State of Industry Report + FY24-25 Performance Evaluation Report; Profit by Pakistan Today (16 Jan 2026, 13 Aug 2026); Business Recorder; Geo News (K-Electric 2005 privatization)

topic: Why Pakistan closed its entire border with Afghanistan — and what it's costing both countries
why_it_works: After October 2025 airstrikes and Taliban retaliation over TTP sanctuaries, Pakistan shut every crossing with Afghanistan — bilateral trade has since fallen 40-53%, costing Pakistani exporters an estimated $177 million a month, and a Qatar-mediated ceasefire collapsed within weeks, so this is a live case study in how a security dispute over an unrecognized border (the Durand Line) turns into a self-inflicted trade war neither side can easily walk back from.
hook_angle: Contradiction/question hook: two countries that need each other's trade routes have voluntarily shut them down over a border neither fully agrees is even the border.
sources: Kabul Now (Jan 2026, trade drop); Afghanistan International (53% trade fall); RFE/RL and NPR (Feb-Jun 2026 border closure reporting); OHCHR (Mar 2026 UN call for peace)
notes: Verify current border status and exact trade-loss figures at drafting time — this is a fast-moving, still-unresolved story as of research date; distinguish Pakistani-exporter losses from total bilateral trade figures before scripting.

topic: The NFC Award: why Pakistan's provinces keep fighting over money that's already supposed to be theirs
why_it_works: Rs8.2 trillion is transferred to provinces every year under a formula meant to end this argument — yet KP is demanding over Rs1 trillion in dues it says it was promised (including a 3% divisible-pool share for the Newly Merged Districts), Balochistan says it's shortchanged too, and experts don't expect the next Award for at least another year — a policy topic most viewers have heard of but few understand well enough to know why the fighting never actually stops.
hook_angle: Question hook: 'Pakistan's provinces get Rs8.2 trillion a year specifically so they'll stop fighting over money. They're still fighting. Why?'
sources: The Nation (27 Feb 2026, Ahsan Iqbal reform call); Pakistan Today (26 Mar 2026); Dawn ('There's nothing smooth about the NFC'); Mettis Global ('The Next NFC Debate'); PRAC policy paper on NFC stalemate
notes: Needs the actual NFC formula breakdown (vertical/horizontal distribution shares) and a primary Ministry of Finance source for the Rs8.2tn and KP's Rs1tn dues claim before scripting.
